output.summary: I added `!layout_ptr->AllConstant()` to the staging condition in GroupedAggregateHashTable::FindOrCreateGroupsInternal. With it, fixed-width group layouts scatter straight into partitioned_data and skip the unpartitioned_data staging and the Repartition on Abandon. The build succeeded and results were correct. It gave no gain. `bench q18`: best 682.7 ms, mine 686.2 ms (+0.5%, within noise). On the isolated `SELECT max(s) FROM (SELECT l_orderkey, sum(l_quantity) s ... GROUP BY l_orderkey)`, warm runs were 610-700 ms before (one cold 980 ms, then 953, 698, 613, 698, 610) and 685-880 ms after (882, 712, 685, 805, 723, 746). So it is not faster and may be a little slower. I skipped the step 1 timers. The end-to-end on/off comparison already showed the staging path is not a cost worth removing.
output.generality: This would have applied to high-cardinality GROUP BYs with fixed-width keys and states, running with many threads and 3+ radix bits. It made no measurable difference on q18. Heap (VARCHAR) layouts were never affected.
output.notes: The other threshold (`< 2` instead of `<= 4` for fixed-width) sends q18's groups the same way, because about 512 new groups per chunk over 128 partitions is 4 per partition. So that variant was in effect tested too. For fixed-width rows, the stage-plus-repartition copy is not a significant part of the sink. This differs from the heap-layout result on q16 (-5%). Q18 sink cost must be elsewhere: hash probe and compare, InitializeStates, the aggregate update, or the scan. A perf or cycle-level breakdown of FindOrCreateGroupsInternal compared with UpdateAggregates is needed before trying another sink-side idea for q18. Runs of `dbe-tool sql` are noisy (±15%), so use bench for decisions.
